problem: Consider the Dirichlet problem $-\nabla \cdot ({\bf A}(x)\nabla u(x)) = f(x)$ in a bounded domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ (with $n \ge 3$), where the symmetric coefficient matrix ${\bf A}(x)$ may not be uniformly elliptic. Let $\lambda(x)$ denote the smallest eigenvalue of ${\bf A}(x)$. To establish local boundedness and H\u00f6lder continuity of the weak solution, it is typically assumed that $\lambda(x)^{-1}$ belongs to a Lebesgue space $L^p(\Omega)$. What is the essentially sharp value of the exponent $p$ as a function of the spatial dimension $n$?
